payload.title: The SUPERIORITY_SCHEMA comment states window_days as the window each side of the paired test reads, while the policy default's _doc and the code define it as the baseline look-back before the EVAL_WINDOW entry with an open-ended candidate window, so one contract is stated twice with two meanings and no pin
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/genesis_policy.py:1062-1066 (comment: window_days is which eval runs each side of the paired test reads)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/data/genesis_policy_default.json:212 (the _doc: window_days is the length of the baseline look-back before the entry; the comparison starts at the entry and has no end)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/agent_eval.py:772-784 (current window is [window_start, open end), previous window is [window_start - window_days, window_start))
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/agent_eval.py:1031-1035 (now = window_start + window_days is only the seam of the split)
payload.rule_violated: One owner per fact (CLAUDE.md single center, PLAN-v2 section 1.2): the meaning of window_days has two statements that differ and no test ties them.
payload.notes: A developer or operator who reads the schema comment concludes that window_days bounds the runs both sides read, so lengthening it widens the candidate's evidence. Under F1.8(a) the candidate side is open-ended from the entry and window_days only sets how far back the baseline reaches, so a wrong expectation about the pre-registered knob follows from the comment while the policy file says the opposite. Close condition: Rewrite the comment above SUPERIORITY_SCHEMA to the meaning in genesis_policy_default.json (or drop the key description and point at the _doc), and add an assertion in the genesis policy tests that the schema comment and the default _doc do not give window_days different meanings, or delete the comment so the _doc is the only statement. Verified at origin/main a81bfa2d6.
